exercises.prompt: What command produces the left half of the floor-function brackets shown here: $\lfloor x \rfloor$?
exercises.explanation: `\lfloor` and `\rfloor` draw the floor-function corner brackets; the analogous `\lceil`/`\rceil` pair draws ceiling brackets instead.

exercises.prompt: Which command stacks a label directly underneath a symbol, as used to write $\underset{n\to\infty}{\lim}$ (placing the limit condition below "lim" instead of using a subscript)?
exercises.explanation: `\underset{below}{main}` stacks `below` directly beneath `main`, commonly used for custom limit conditions or annotated relations. `\overset` does the mirror image above; `\underbrace` instead draws a labeled brace under an expression; `\below` isn't a real LaTeX command.

exercises.prompt: Write the LaTeX source for this labeled arrow (a function f mapping A to B), matching this target exactly: $$A \xrightarrow{f} B$$ Then reveal and compare.
exercises.explanation: `\xrightarrow{label}` draws a rightward arrow with `label` typeset above it — common in function notation and commutative diagrams; `\xleftarrow` mirrors it pointing left.
